doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Woody Herman and the war years
title: Harlem after hours and the term offay
summary: He recalls the Herman band's swing, and Black musicians taking him to Minton's and Harlem bars, where Slingshot explained hijive talk.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Chubby Jackson, Bill Harris, Flip Phillips, there was quite a crew in that band.
Well everybody at that time thought it was one of the swingingest bands. Especially for Offays. Do you know what Offays were?
Yes I do. Those white guys can really swing, huh?

Oh I had a lot of black players, they used to come in, like they would take me down the hall and then where Minton’s was, and then there was another place down there. All the guys used to sit in, like the Basie band, not the band, but guys in the band you know, and they’d bring me down the hall and they liked me, I don’t know. They’d just take me around, they’d protect me.

I don’t know. But they were very nice to me, and they’d show me, they’d tell me, so that’s why I know about offays, because in one of these places, this was about four in the morning. I’d get through at three, and they’d meet me somewhere down around 125th Street, and we’d go around for a couple of hours. But at the bar, sometimes I was the only white guy there. And these guys would — this one guy’s name was Slingshot. I said, © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

“Slingshot, this guy’s banging me in the back all the time.” He says, “Let’s change places.” So he got over there, and nobody — so he says, “Listen to them,” and they would torture me, and say, “Hey go on there, rubber band.” He says they’re not talking about nothing, they’re hijiving. Don’t you want to hijive with them? You know, just talking. The rubber means automobile. And they had names for each thing. So he was explaining what they were doing. He said, “They ain’t talking about nothing.
And he said they were hijiving.
Yeah. Hi jiving. And he says, like they say, that offay, he says, that means you.
